mascot: Seed Scout Samir — a curious young botanist with a magnifying glass, a notebook and a pouch full of seeds

slides.title: A Seed Is a Baby Plant's Box 🌰
slides.text: Every seed is a tiny box of life! Outside is the SEED COAT for protection. Inside is a BABY PLANT waiting to grow, plus stored FOOD to feed it. Beans, wheat, rice — all began as seeds!
slides.spoken: A seed protects a baby plant and its food inside a tough coat.

slides.title: Germination: The Seed Wakes Up! 🌱
slides.text: When a seed gets WATER, AIR and WARMTH, it wakes up and sprouts — this is GERMINATION! The root comes out first, then a tiny shoot reaches up.
slides.spoken: Water, air and warmth wake the seed — that is germination.

slides.title: What Seeds Need to Sprout 💧
slides.text: A seed in a packet on the shelf stays asleep. Give it water, air and warmth and it sprouts! Keep it bone-dry or ice-cold and it waits. Farmers store seeds dry for this reason.
slides.spoken: No water, no sprouting — dry seeds stay asleep.

slides.title: Seeds Travel! 🌬️
slides.text: Seeds travel to new places to grow! Light winged seeds of drumstick fly on the WIND. Coconuts float away on WATER. Mangoes are carried by ANIMALS that eat the fruit. Some pods even BURST and fling seeds!
slides.spoken: Wind, water, animals and bursting pods carry seeds to new places.

slides.title: From Seed to Plant 🌳
slides.text: Root grows DOWN to hold the plant and drink water. Shoot grows UP towards the sun. Leaves open and make food. Give it time — a tiny seed becomes a huge tree!
slides.spoken: Root down, shoot up, leaves make food — a plant is born!

challenges.question: What is the outer covering of a seed called?
challenges.hint: It is the seed's tough protective box!
challenges.misconception: The seed coat protects the baby plant inside.

challenges.question: Which thing does NOT help a seed sprout?
challenges.hint: Three things wake a seed. Which one keeps it asleep?
challenges.misconception: Seeds need water, air and warmth. Ice-cold keeps them asleep.

challenges.question: Which part comes out FIRST from a sprouting seed?
challenges.hint: It grows DOWN to drink water and hold the plant!
challenges.misconception: The root comes out first during germination.

challenges.question: A coconut floats across the sea and grows on a new shore. It travels by ______.
challenges.hint: Coconuts are made to float on waves!
challenges.misconception: Coconuts travel by floating on water.

challenges.question: The light winged seeds of drumstick travel far on the ______.
challenges.hint: Wings catch the breeze and fly!
challenges.misconception: Winged seeds are carried far by the wind.

challenges.question: Sort each seed by how it travels!
challenges.hint: Light and winged flies on wind; buoyant things float on water.
challenges.misconception: Drumstick and madhaar seeds fly on wind. Coconuts and lotus seeds float on water.

challenges.question: Inside every seed is a tiny ______ waiting to grow.
challenges.hint: The seed's secret passenger — a mini plant!
challenges.misconception: A baby plant sleeps inside every healthy seed.

challenges.question: Farmers keep seeds DRY before sowing. If seeds get wet, they may ______.
challenges.hint: Remember what makes a seed wake up — don't wake it too soon!
challenges.misconception: Dry seeds stay asleep. Water would make them sprout early or rot in storage.
